en: The Vajravidāraṇā Dhāraṇī:
The Noble Dhāraṇī Named Vajravidāraṇā.
Om! Homage to the Blessed One, the Noble Vajravidāraṇā!
Thus have I heard: at one time the Blessed One was dwelling among the Vajras.
Having empowered his entire body as being composed of vajra, and with the majestic power of the Buddha, Vajrapāṇi entered the vajra-samādhi.

Then, through the majestic power of all the Buddhas, Vajrapāṇi spoke the Vajrasāra, which had arisen from the empowerment of all the Buddhas and the empowerment of all the Bodhisattvas, and was produced by the Great Wrathful One.

It is indestructible, indivisible, true, firm, stable, unimpeded everywhere, unconquered everywhere, causing the flight of all beings, causing the destruction of all beings, causing the severing of all spells, causing the paralyzing of all spells,

causing the shattering of all rites, causing the dispersal of all rites, causing the eradication of all planetary influences, causing the liberation from all planetary influences, and causing the summoning of all spirits.

This mantra, which subdues all bhūtas, which brings one to the culmination of all vidyā-mantra rites, which grants success to those who have not yet attained it and preserves the success of those who have, which bestows all desires, which provides protection for all sentient beings, and which performs pacification (śāntika), nourishment (pauṣṭika), the immobilization (stambhana) of all sentient beings, and the delusion (mohana) of all sentient beings— this mantra...
Through the power of the Buddha, the mighty Vajrapāṇi, lord of the yakṣas, replied:
"Oṃ! Homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi!"
To the Great Yakṣa General:
namely—Oṃ truṭa truṭa, tear asunder, tear asunder; burst, burst, shatter, shatter; whirl, whirl, cause to whirl, cause to whirl;
awaken, awaken all sentient beings, bring them to full awakening, bring them to full awakening; roam, roam!

Confuse, confuse all beings! *Kuṭa kuṭa*, crush, crush all enemies! *Ghaṭa ghaṭa*, assemble, assemble all vidyās! O Vajra, shatter with the vajra! O Vajra, vajra, strike! O Vajra, vajra, trample! O Vajra, vajra, churn!
Svāhā to the Blue Vajra of the Terrifying Laughter, the Excellent Vajra!
Oṃ he fullu nirufullu nigṛhṇa kullu mili cullu kuru kullu vajravijayāya svāhā!
Oṃ kilikīlāya svāhā!
Oṃ kaṭa kaṭa maṭa maṭa raṭa raṭa moṭana pramoṭanāya svāhā!
Oṃ cara nicara hara hara sara sara māraya vajravidāraṇāya svāhā / Oṃ chinda chinda bhinda bhinda mahākilikīlāya svāhā / Oṃ bandha bandha krodha krodha vajrakilikīlāya svāhā /
Oṃ curu curu caṇḍakilikīlāya svāhā!
Oṃ trāsaya trāsaya vajrakilikīlāya svāhā!
Oṃ hara hara vajradharāya svāhā!
Oṃ prahara prahara vajraprabhañjanāya svāhā!
Oṃ mati-sthiravajra śruti-sthiravajra prati-sthiravajra mahāvajra apratihata-vajra amogha-vajra ehi-vajra śīghraṃ vajrāya svāhā!
Oṃ dhara dhara dhiri dhiri dhuru dhuru sarva-vajrakula-āvartāya svāhā!
Kill so-and-so, phaṭ!
Om, homage to all Vajras!
O you who possess all power, turn back [the forces], O Great Power, Kaṭabala, Tatale, Acale, Maṇḍalamaye, Ativajra, Mahābale, Vegaraṇa, Ajite! Blaze, blaze! Tiṭi tiṭi ti(piṃ)!
Ṅgale daha daha tejovati tili tili bandha bandha mahābale vajrāṅkuśajvālāya svāhā! Oṃ, homage to the Three Jewels! Homage to Caṇḍavajrapāṇi, the great general of the yakṣas!

Namely: Oṃ hara hara vajra, matha matha vajra, dhuna dhuna vajra, daha daha vajra, paca paca vajra, dhara dhara vajra, dhāraya dhāraya vajra, dāruṇa dāruṇa vajra, chinda chinda vajra, bhinda bhinda vajra, hūṃ phaṭ!
Oṃ namaścaṇḍavajrakrodhāya / Oṃ hulu hulu tiṣṭha tiṣṭha bandha bandha hana hana amṛte hūṃ phaṭ / This is the heart-mantra, the near-heart mantra, and the root mantra.
Having brought about the destruction of all evil and the eradication of all suffering,
it is the root of all mantras and is adorned with every glory.
Having become one whose senses are stilled, [he beholds those] whose support is lost and whose life-force is destroyed,
who are surrounded by misfortune and from whom the deities have turned away.
A beloved woman suffers during separation from her husband; one afflicted by malevolent planets likewise experiences the mutual loss of wealth as well as calamity.
For those afflicted by grief and exhaustion, as well as by fear and calamity;
or for those tormented by planets and constellations, or by terrible *kākhorda* spells and malevolent spirits;
one sees inauspicious things in dreams, characterized by an abundance of grief and exhaustion.
And this supreme sūtra should be heard by one who is well-bathed and pure;
let those who hear this profound sūtra, which is the domain of the Buddhas, listen.
With clear minds and joyful hearts, adorned with clean garments,
they [overcome] all those evil-minded ones and most terrible calamities.
His vital energy shall be pacified, he shall attain everything in its entirety,
his lifespan and merit shall increase, and he shall be liberated from all sins.
Having filled a golden vessel with water, along with jewels, mustard seeds, dūrvā grass, gems, unbroken grains (akṣata), sandalwood, and flowers tied with vajra-knots;
Both the jar and the silver [vessel] should be perfumed with a clean cloth twenty-one times, or likewise one hundred and eight times.
The king who always bathes while reciting the Vidyārana mantra,
and who acts in this manner constantly, for him prosperity and auspiciousness are attained.
Thus spoke the Blessed One, and the monks, that entire assembly, and the world with its gods, humans, asuras, garuḍas, and gandharvas, rejoiced in what the Blessed One had said.
The Noble Dhāraṇī named Vajravidāraṇā is completed.
